claim: Before anything is run, LLM-written research ideas are judged more novel than expert ideas by blind expert reviewers (4.84 human vs 5.64 AI vs 5.81 AI+rerank, 1-10, per review; AI slightly lower on feasibility, n.s.).
agent_test: Not worth re-testing; use as a prior that a model's own novelty rating of its ideas is inflated.

claim: Pre-execution appraisal of LLM ideas over-rates them: after 100+ hours of expert execution, AI ideas dropped about 1.0 (novelty) to 1.9 (effectiveness) points while human ideas stayed flat; ranking flipped on several metrics (flip itself not significant, N=43). Gap search: ideation-to-execution correlations are about zero (AI ideas Pearson r overall -0.092, excitement -0.321; human overall 0.158), no replication outside NLP found.
agent_test: Take the agent's candidate ideas, record a model score before running, run each at equal token budget with a cheap probe, and compare score-vs-outcome correlation. Expect weak correlation.

claim: Models and humans are near chance at judging which idea is better without outcome training: human split-half agreement 56.1%, best LLM judge 53.3% (others 43-52%), zero-shot GPT-4.1 51.9% on predicting which of two idea pairs works, majority of five experts 48.9%.
agent_test: Ask the agent to pick the better of two of its own ideas; compare accuracy against the executed result on 50+ pairs at equal tokens. Compare with a run-a-probe selector.

claim: Appraisal accuracy can be raised by outcome-trained predictors (fine-tuned GPT-4.1 + full-paper retrieval 77% in-distribution, 63.6% on fresh unpublished ideas, 64.4% vs 48.9% for experts on NLP subset), but it falls out of distribution and needs thousands of labelled pairs. Gap search (2026): GPT-5 zero-shot reaches 57.7 to 61.1% on 11,488 benchmark idea pairs (consistency-aware), an 8B model fine-tuned on outcomes reaches 77.1%; trained models transfer poorly cross-domain (about 45 to 49%).
agent_test: Log idea features and executed outcomes in the agent's own runs; check after N>=100 whether a simple logistic predictor beats chance.

claim: Overgeneration hits a diversity ceiling: of 4000 seed ideas per topic only about 5% (about 200) were non-duplicates at cosine 0.8, so sampling more ideas from one model does not widen the candidate set.
agent_test: Sample 20 ideas at equal tokens, dedup by embedding in code, report number of distinct directions; compare with seeded-different-schema generation.

claim: A pursuit rule that uses a code-computed score on held-out data works: HypoGeniC UCB-style bank beats few-shot by 3.3-31.7% and fine-tuning by 11.6-12.1% on two real sets; bank updating adds 0.7-8.1%.
agent_test: On a task with a checkable score, compare UCB allocation across K candidate hypotheses against uniform allocation at equal tokens.

claim: Best-first or tournament selection by an external measured score is a deployed pursuit policy (AI Scientist-v2 tree search: 1 of 3 papers reached the workshop acceptance band at 6.33; co-scientist Elo rises with compute), but the Elo judge is model-made and the v2 sample is 3. Gap search: adaptive allocation beats uniform when the score is informative (up to +11 points on MATH-500 at equal budget; Zuo and Zhu). On ideas, only proxy-judged evidence: random-k or MMR-k subset refinement beats refine-all on cost per strong idea (Zhang 2026, single author, LLM judges).
agent_test: Compare a tournament judged by the model against a tournament judged by executed checks, at equal tokens, on a checkable benchmark.

claim: Self-critique without an external signal does not help discovery, but real outcome feedback does (DiscoveryBench: ReAct/self-critic planning no clear gain over CodeGen, best about 25%; Reflexion with oracle feedback helps; POPPER shows agent self-checks inflate Type-I error to 0.145-0.248 at alpha 0.1 until wrapped in sequential falsification).
agent_test: Revise with and without real execution output at equal tokens; measure false-accept rate.

claim: Keyword-search novelty gates over-accept: all 10 generated and 2 seed ideas were labelled novel in an independent test of the AI Scientist, including well-known ones; 5 of 12 experiments failed from coding errors; 4 of 7 manuscripts had wrong or hallucinated numbers. Gap search: checkers that read retrieved papers do much better. Retrieve-and-rerank with 15 expert examples gets 0.81 accuracy (n=32 test); keyword and snippet retrieval alone recover 5 to 9% of not-novel cases vs 89.66% for full system.
agent_test: Run the S0 novelty/known-solution check on 20 known-answer items and report false-novel rate; require a read of retrieved text, not keyword hit.

claim: Staged screening is a cheap preliminary appraisal that works at corpus scale: MOOSE-Chem retrieves over 75% of ground-truth inspirations within the top 4% of the corpus (83.7% at window 15/keep 3; 76.8% to 88.9% by corpus size), and SciMON's retrieve-compare-revise loop raised novelty in about half of ideas per round.
agent_test: Funnel with code-run tournament screening vs one-shot ranking for picking relevant premises, at equal tokens.

claim: Held-out or out-of-domain fit with model priors plus code-fitted parameters beats either alone (LLM-SR OOD NMSE about 0.0037 vs baselines above 1; ablating prior knowledge worsened NMSE to 0.18 OOD).
agent_test: Pass criterion on held-out extrapolation versus in-sample fit on a function-discovery task.

claim: Weak (promise) versus strong (acceptance) evaluation, and pursuit as a third context, have no direct empirical test; support is historical reconstruction only. Heuristics are sufficient not necessary and carry systematic bias.
agent_test: A/B a two-tier gate (cheap probe then full check) against a single full check at equal tokens; measure budget wasted on dead ideas.

claim: Model-based social-epistemology results on sharing and diversity are model-dependent: Zollman effect (more communication can hurt), Weisberg-Muldoon mavericks (criticised, partly restored), Borg et al. (sharing does not hurt). No data from real labs or LLMs. Gap search: in LLM debate networks isolation was worst (63.9% vs 67.7% fully connected, GPT-3.5, 100 MATH questions); no Zollman-style harm from sharing seen, but early isolation was not tested.
agent_test: Run K branches with isolated vs shared early answers at equal tokens; measure distinct final answers and accuracy.

claim: Self-scores that no transition reads are decoration: the AI Scientist's interestingness/feasibility/novelty numbers are not used downstream; only the binary novel flag is.
agent_test: Ablate any score in the schema that drives no branch; confirm no accuracy change.

claim: LLM paper reviewers reach roughly human level on accept/reject (65% vs 66% balanced accuracy; 70% vs 73% raw accuracy; F1 0.57 vs 0.49) only for finished papers with a tuned ensemble; this does not transfer to idea-stage judging (K03).
agent_test: Compare the same judge on finished work versus on early ideas against executed outcomes.

claim: Open-ended data-driven discovery remains hard: best DiscoveryBench system 25%; biology 0%, engineering 7%; 30% of human replications did not reproduce.
agent_test: Use only tasks with a checkable answer when measuring the pursuit gate.

claim: Hanson-style abduction (a surprise signal justifies searching a hypothesis class) is endorsed in the philosophy literature but criticised as too permissive for ranking candidates (Harman) and historically thin (Lugg).
agent_test: Trigger idea search on check-failure or attempt-disagreement versus on a timer; compare tokens to correct answer.

claim: Ideation score does not predict execution score: across 43 executed projects, ideation-vs-execution Pearson r for AI ideas is -0.019 (novelty), -0.321 (excitement), 0.172 (effectiveness), -0.092 (overall); for human ideas -0.084, 0.205, 0.022, 0.158.
agent_test: Compute rank correlation of the agent's pre-run idea scores with probe outcomes on its own runs; expect near zero.

claim: A cheap fixed-budget allocation rule beats uniform allocation when its score is informative (bandit elimination: up to +11.10 points on MATH-500), but no test shows it on research ideas scored by a weak judge; proxy-only evidence says refining a random or diversity-selected subset (MMR-k, 23.70 strong ideas) beats refining all.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare uniform, random-k, successive halving by probe score, and MMR-k on 20 own candidates, scored by an executed check.

claim: A novelty gate that reads reranked retrieved papers works far better than keyword checks, but expert-labelled evidence is tiny (n=32, accuracy 0.81, kappa 0.59) and one non-LLM alternative is validated only on a recency-and-citation proxy.
agent_test: Check the agent's known-vs-novel calls on 30 hand-labelled ideas with and without reranked retrieval.

claim: No controlled LLM test of Darden-style schema instantiation or Nickles-style generative justification at equal tokens exists. The closest, a Hempel/Salmon explanation scaffold (DN-Hypo-Pipeline), beats direct prompting with 3 explananda, but compares 5 proposals to 1.
agent_test: Run scaffolded generation vs best-of-N plain generation at equal tokens, scored by executed probes.

claim: Whether ideation quality seen by LLM judges survives execution (LiveIdeaBench-type findings: idea score vs general intelligence r=0.357, CI 0.022 to 0.621) is untested; all scoring there is by an LLM panel.
agent_test: Not needed; use as caution against choosing generators by reasoning benchmark.

claim: Staged gates exist in agent systems (AI Scientist-v2 four stages; EarlyEval cuts 26% of SWE-bench steps for about 1 point of resolve-rate error), but no study measures whether a two-tier weak/strong gate saves budget for research ideas.
agent_test: Ablate the stage-1 probe: same ideas with and without it at equal total tokens.
